claims.population: Awka has an estimated population of 301,657 as of the 2006 Nigerian census; the two LGAs of Awka South and North had an estimated population of 430,200 in 2022.
claims.climate: The monsoon winds create six months of heavy tropical rains between April and July, followed by a short dry period in August lasting two to three weeks, with rain resuming in September and October; five months of dryness from November to March are marked by the harmattan.
claims.crafts: The town became known for metal working, and its blacksmiths were prized throughout the region for making farming implements, dane guns and ceremonial items such as Oji and Ngwuagilija.
claims.markets: Awka, like most Nigerian cities, is defined by large rudimentary informal markets where everything from basic food produce to clothes, cosmetics and household items is sold; the largest, Eke Awka, houses an estimated 5,000 lock-up shops and stalls.
claims.tertiary: Awka hosts two primary universities of tertiary education, Nnamdi Azikiwe University and Paul University.
